questions.sectionHeading: Section I (25 marks). Allow about 1 hour for this section.
questions.stem: Evaluate the significance of audience in the production of history. Use Sources A and B and at least ONE other source to support your argument.
questions.stimulus:
Source A: an extract from Jorma Kalela, Making History: The Historian and Uses of the Past, 2012. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2020 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2020-hsc-history-extension.pdf

Source B: an extract from Jerome de Groot, Consuming History, 2016. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2020 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2020-hsc-history-extension.pdf
assessedOn: demonstrate knowledge and understanding of relevant issues of historiography
use relevant sources to support your argument
present a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

criteria.text: Provides a critical evaluation of the significance of audience in the production of history ; Supports arguments with integrated and explicit references to Sources A and B, and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates extensive knowledge, clear understanding and critical insight into relevant historiographical issues raised in Sources A and B ; Presents a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

Provides an effective evaluation of the significance of audience in the production of history ; Supports arguments with explicit references to Sources A and B, and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates thorough knowledge and clear understanding of relevant historiographical issues raised in Sources A and B ; Presents a logical and cohesive response

Provides a sound evaluation of the significance of audience in the production of history ; Makes references to Sources A and B and at least ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates sound knowledge and understanding of historiographical issues raised in Sources A and/or B ; Presents a coherent response

Provides a limited response addressing the significance of audience in the production of history ; Makes limited references to Sources A and B and possibly ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates limited knowledge and understanding of historiographical issues ; Presents a limited response

Demonstrates minimal knowledge of the significance of audience in the production of history ; Makes minimal references to Sources A and/or B and possibly ONE other relevant source ; Demonstrates minimal knowledge of historiographical issues ; Presents isolated observations

questions.sectionHeading: Section II (25 marks). Allow about 1 hour for this section.
questions.stem: To what extent does historical debate inform our understanding of the past? In your response, make explicit reference to Source C and TWO areas of debate in your case study. Identify your case study at the beginning of your answer.
questions.stimulus: Source C: an extract from John Lewis Gaddis, The Landscape of History: How Historians Map the Past, 2002. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2020 HSC History Extension paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2025-05/2020-hsc-history-extension.pdf
assessedOn: demonstrate knowledge and understanding of an appropriate case study
engage with the historiography of the areas of debate selected for discussion
present a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

criteria.text: Demonstrates extensive knowledge, clear understanding and critical insight of the extent to which historical debate informs our understanding of the past ; Demonstrates highly effective use of Source C within the historiography of TWO areas of debate in the chosen case study ; Presents a comprehensive, logical and sustained response

Demonstrates thorough knowledge and clear understanding of the extent to which historical debate informs our understanding of the past ; Demonstrates effective use of Source C within the historiography of TWO areas of debate in the chosen case study ; Presents a logical and cohesive response

Demonstrates sound knowledge and some understanding of how historical debate informs our understanding of the past ; Demonstrates sound use of Source C within the historiography of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Presents a coherent response

Demonstrates limited knowledge and understanding of how historical debate informs our understanding of the past ; Demonstrates limited use of Source C with reference to the historiography of at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Presents a limited response

Demonstrates minimal knowledge of how historical debate informs our understanding of the past ; Demonstrates minimal use of Source C with reference to at least ONE area of debate in the chosen case study ; Presents isolated observations
